metadata.title: Cocliques in the Kneser graph on (n-1,n)-flags of PG(2n,q)

nodes.name: (n-1,n)-flag and opposite flags
nodes.statement: In PG(2n,q), an (n-1,n)-flag is a pair (A,B) where A is an (n-1)-space contained in an n-space B. Two flags (A_1,B_1) and (A_2,B_2) are opposite if A_1 ∩ B_2 = A_2 ∩ B_1 = ∅.

nodes.name: Graph Γ_{2n}
nodes.statement: For n ≥ 2, Γ_{2n} is the graph whose vertices are the (n-1,n)-flags of PG(2n,q), with two vertices adjacent if the corresponding flags are opposite.

nodes.name: Gaussian coefficient
nodes.statement: The Gaussian coefficient [b choose a]_q is defined as the product ∏_{i=1}^{a} (q^{b-a+i}-1)/(q^i-1) for 0 ≤ a ≤ b, and 0 otherwise. It is a q-polynomial of degree a(b-a).

nodes.name: Example 1.1 — Large coclique constructions
nodes.statement: Two dual families of large cocliques of Γ_{2n} are constructed: (a) Fix a hyperplane H and a point or (2n-2)-space X incident with H; take all flags (A,B) with B ⊆ H or A incident with both X and H. (b) Fix a point P and a hyperplane or line X through P; take all flags (A,B) with P ⊆ A or B incident with both X and P. All four constructions yield cocliques of the same size.

nodes.name: Function f(n,q)
nodes.statement: f(n,q) = 3[n choose 1]_q [2n-2 choose n-2]_q if n ≥ 4 and q ≥ 4, and f(n,q) = q^5 + 2q^4 + 3q^3 + 2q^2 + q + 1 if n = 3.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.3 — Main Theorem
nodes.statement: For n ≥ 3 and q large enough, every maximal coclique F of Γ_{2n} falls into exactly one of three categories: (a) F has size [2n choose n-1]_q [n+1 choose 1]_q + [2n-1 choose n-1]_q q^n and is one of the constructions from Example 1.1; (b) |F| ≤ [2n choose n-1]_q [n+1 choose 1]_q + f(n,q)·q^n and there is a hyperplane H with all flags (A,B) with B ⊆ H in F, or a point P with all flags (A,B) with P ⊆ A in F; (c) |F| is at most O(q^{n²+n-2}).
assumptions: q is large enough compared to n
F is a maximal coclique of Γ_{2n}
conclusions: Either |F| = [2n choose n-1]_q [n+1 choose 1]_q + [2n-1 choose n-1]_q q^n and F is as in Example 1.1
Or |F| ≤ [2n choose n-1]_q [n+1 choose 1]_q + f(n,q)·q^n and all flags with B in a hyperplane H (or P in all A) belong to F
Or |F| = O(q^{n²+n-2})

nodes.name: Corollary 1.4 — Chromatic number of Γ_{2n}
nodes.statement: For q large enough, the chromatic number of Γ_{2n} is (q^{n+2}-1)/(q-1) - q.
assumptions: q is large enough
Γ_{2n} is the Kneser graph on (n-1,n)-flags of PG(2n,q)
conclusions: The chromatic number of Γ_{2n} equals (q^{n+2}-1)/(q-1) - q

nodes.name: Notation 2.2 — Red and yellow spaces
nodes.statement: An n-space B or (n-1)-space A occurring in [n+1 choose 1]_q flags of F is called F-red (or red). If it occurs in at most [n choose 1]_q flags but at least 1, it is called F-yellow (or yellow).

nodes.name: Lemma 2.1 — Possible weights of n-spaces
nodes.statement: If B is an n-space occurring in a flag of the maximal coclique F, then the number of flags containing B is [k choose 1]_q for some k ∈ {1,...,n+1}. This number equals [n+1 choose 1]_q iff every flag (A',B') in F satisfies A' ∩ B ≠ ∅.
assumptions: F is a maximal coclique of Γ_{2n}
B is an n-space occurring in a flag of F
conclusions: The number of flags in F containing B is [k choose 1]_q for some k ∈ {1,...,n+1}
The count is [n+1 choose 1]_q if and only if every flag (A',B') in F satisfies A' ∩ B ≠ ∅

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Shows by maximality that if all flags meet B then all (n-1)-subspaces of B are in F giving [n+1 choose 1]_q flags; otherwise the skew flags force a constraint via their intersection points, whose span S has dimension s, yielding [n-s choose 1]_q flags containing B.

nodes.name: Corollary 2.3 — Possible weights of (n-1)-spaces
nodes.statement: If A is an (n-1)-space occurring in a flag of F, then the number of flags containing A is [k choose 1]_q for some k ∈ {1,...,n+1}. This equals [n+1 choose 1]_q iff every flag (A',B') in F satisfies B' ∩ A ≠ ∅.
assumptions: F is a maximal coclique of Γ_{2n}
A is an (n-1)-space occurring in a flag of F
conclusions: The number of flags in F containing A is [k choose 1]_q for some k ∈ {1,...,n+1}
The count is [n+1 choose 1]_q if and only if every flag (A',B') in F satisfies B' ∩ A ≠ ∅

nodes.name: Lemma 2.4 — Red spaces intersect
nodes.statement: Any two red (n-1)-spaces always meet. Any two red n-spaces are not in general position (i.e., they intersect in at least a line).
assumptions: F is a maximal coclique of Γ_{2n}
The spaces in question are red with respect to F
conclusions: Any two red (n-1)-spaces intersect
Any two red n-spaces intersect in at least a line

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.4
nodes.statement: If two red n-spaces B_1, B_2 meet only in a point, one can find (n-1)-subspaces A_1 ⊂ B_1, A_2 ⊂ B_2 with A_1 ∩ B_2 = A_2 ∩ B_1 = ∅, contradicting the characterization of red spaces from Lemma 2.1.

nodes.name: Result 2.5 — EKR + Hilton-Milner for vector spaces
nodes.statement: Let C be a set of pairwise intersecting (n-1)-spaces of PG(2n,q) with n ≥ 3, q ≥ 3. Then either |C| ≤ [2n choose n-1]_q - q^{n(n-1)}[n choose 1]_q, or there exists a point P incident with every (n-1)-space in C.
assumptions: C is a set of pairwise intersecting (n-1)-spaces of PG(2n,q)
conclusions: Either |C| ≤ [2n choose n-1]_q - q^{n(n-1)}[n choose 1]_q
Or there exists a point P incident with all (n-1)-spaces in C

nodes.name: Remark 2.6 — Degree bound
nodes.statement: The quantity [2n choose n-1]_q - q^{n(n-1)}[n choose 1]_q is a polynomial in q of degree at most n²-2.

nodes.name: Corollary 2.7 — Number of red spaces
nodes.statement: For a maximal coclique F of Γ_{2n} with n ≥ 3: either the number of red (n-1)-spaces is O(q^{n²-2}), or there is a point P such that every (n-1)-space through P is red. Dually, either the number of red n-spaces is O(q^{n²-2}), or there is a hyperplane H with every n-space in H being red.
assumptions: F is a maximal coclique of Γ_{2n}
conclusions: Either the number of red (n-1)-spaces is O(q^{n²-2}), or there is a point P with every (n-1)-space through P red
Either the number of red n-spaces is O(q^{n²-2}), or there is a hyperplane H with every n-space in H red

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.7
nodes.statement: If the number of red (n-1)-spaces exceeds the Hilton-Milner bound, Result 2.5 gives a common point P. Then any flag's n-space meets P, and by maximality every (n-1)-space through P is red.

nodes.name: Result 3.1 — EKR and Hilton-Milner for PG(2n-1,q)
nodes.statement: (a) A largest family of pairwise intersecting (n-1)-spaces in PG(2n-1,q) has size [2n-1 choose n-1]_q and all spaces pass through a common point or hyperplane. (b) Without a common point or hyperplane, the family has size < f(n,q).
assumptions: C is a set of pairwise intersecting (n-1)-spaces in PG(2n-1,q)
conclusions: If C is maximum, |C| = [2n-1 choose n-1]_q and all spaces share a point or hyperplane
If no common point or hyperplane exists, then |C| < f(n,q)

nodes.name: Lemma 3.2 — Many red n-spaces case
nodes.statement: If F is a maximal coclique of Γ_{2n} with n ≥ 3 and the number of red n-spaces is not O(q^{n²-2}), then F is as in Example 1.1(a), or |F| ≤ [2n choose n-1]_q [n+1 choose 1]_q + f(n,q)·q^n and there is a hyperplane H such that F contains all flags (A,B) with B ⊆ H.
assumptions: F is a maximal coclique of Γ_{2n}
The number of red n-spaces is not O(q^{n²-2})
conclusions: F is as described in Example 1.1(a), or
|F| ≤ [2n choose n-1]_q [n+1 choose 1]_q + f(n,q)·q^n with a hyperplane H such that all flags with B ⊆ H belong to F

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: By Corollary 2.7 there is a hyperplane H with all n-spaces in H red. Every flag's (n-1)-space must lie in H. Flags with B not in H have pairwise intersecting (n-1)-spaces in H, so Result 3.1 gives either a common point/(2n-2)-space (yielding Example 1.1(a)) or at most f(n,q) such (n-1)-spaces, bounding the total.

nodes.name: Result 4.1 — Erdős-Matching Theorem for vector spaces
nodes.statement: For n ≥ 3 and q large enough, if a family C of (n-1)-spaces in PG(2n,q) contains no s+1 pairwise skew (n-1)-spaces, then |C| ≤ s·[2n choose n-1]_q.
assumptions: q large enough compared to n
C is a family of (n-1)-spaces in PG(2n,q) with no s+1 pairwise skew members
conclusions: |C| ≤ s·[2n choose n-1]_q

nodes.name: Lemma 4.2 — Many pairwise skew yellow spaces
nodes.statement: If the number of red spaces is O(q^{n²-2}), then |F| is O(q^{n²+n-2}), or there are at least n+1 pairwise skew yellow (n-1)-spaces, or at least n+1 yellow n-spaces in pairwise general position.
assumptions: F is a maximal coclique of Γ_{2n} with n ≥ 3
The number of red spaces is O(q^{n²-2})
conclusions: |F| = O(q^{n²+n-2}), or
There exist n+1 pairwise skew yellow (n-1)-spaces, or
There exist n+1 yellow n-spaces in pairwise general position

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement: Red spaces contribute O(q^{n²+n-2}) flags. If |F| exceeds this, the number of yellow spaces exceeds O(q^{n²-1}). By the Erdős-Matching theorem (Result 4.1), if at most n yellow (n-1)-spaces are pairwise skew, then there are at most n·[2n choose n-1]_q = O(q^{n²-1}) such spaces, a contradiction.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.3 — Few n-spaces meet n+1 pairwise skew (n-1)-spaces
nodes.statement: If A_1,...,A_{n+1} are pairwise skew (n-1)-spaces of PG(2n,q), the number of n-spaces meeting every A_i is O(q^{n²-1}).
assumptions: A_1,...,A_{n+1} are pairwise skew (n-1)-spaces of PG(2n,q)
conclusions: The number of n-spaces intersecting all A_i is O(q^{n²-1})

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement: Fix intersection subspaces P_i = B ∩ A_i with dimensions s_i. Case 1: some span <P_1,...,P_{i'}> meets A_{i'+1}; a detailed dimension count shows the degree of the q-polynomial bound is at most n²-1. Case 2: no such span meets the next A; then all P_i must be points and B is their unique span, again giving O(q^{n²-1}).

nodes.name: Lemma 4.4 — Yellow n-spaces meet almost all (n-1)-spaces
nodes.statement: For a maximal coclique F of Γ_{2n} with n ≥ 3, if B is a yellow n-space, then the number of flags (A',B') in F with pairwise distinct n-spaces and A' ∩ B = ∅ is O(q^{n²-1}).
assumptions: F is a maximal coclique of Γ_{2n} with n ≥ 3
B is a yellow n-space
conclusions: The number of flags (A',B') in F with distinct n-spaces and A' ∩ B = ∅ is O(q^{n²-1})

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.4
nodes.statement: Since B is yellow, some (A,B) ∈ F exists. Any flag (A',B') with A' ∩ B = ∅ forces B' ∩ B to be a point of A. For a fixed point P in A, the n-spaces B' through P that pairwise avoid being in general position are bounded by [2n-1 choose n-1]_q via the EKR theorem in the quotient of P. Summing over [n choose 1]_q points gives O(q^{n²-1}).

nodes.name: Proposition 4.5 — Few red spaces bound
nodes.statement: If n ≥ 3 and F is a maximal coclique of Γ_{2n} with the number of red spaces O(q^{n²-2}), then |F| = O(q^{n²+n-2}).
assumptions: F is a maximal coclique of Γ_{2n}
The number of red spaces is O(q^{n²-2})

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.5
nodes.proof_strategy: combining skew spaces with meeting bounds
nodes.statement: Red spaces contribute O(q^{n²+n-2}) flags. By Lemma 4.2, there are n+1 pairwise skew yellow (n-1)-spaces A_1,...,A_{n+1} (or dual). By Lemma 4.4, flags with B skew to some A_i contribute O(q^{n²+n-2}). By Lemma 4.3, n-spaces meeting all A_i number O(q^{n²-1}), yielding O(q^{n²+n-2}) additional flags. Total is O(q^{n²+n-2}).
